claims.text: A CALPHAD-based high-throughput computational method can efficiently screen thousands of alloy compositions.
The method can identify alloys having specified BCC and L2₁ phase fractions.
The method can identify alloys having melting temperatures suitable for high-temperature applications.
The computational screening is applicable at Tm, 0.8Tm, and 0.5Tm.
The composition space can be screened using a 5 at.% step size.
The applicable composition range requires Al below 25 at.%.
The applicable composition range requires Mn above 15 at.%.
The contents of the other alloying elements remain unchanged within the stated composition range.
The accuracy of the method depends on the thermodynamic database.
Relative to current experimental and computational methods, the intervention will improve the accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature.
Relative to current experimental and computational methods, the intervention will improve the accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining enthalpy of fusion.
Relative to current experimental and computational methods, the intervention will improve the accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining entropy of fusion.
Relative to current experimental and computational methods, the intervention will improve the accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining volume change upon melting.
Relative to current experimental and computational methods, the intervention will improve the accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining liquid thermodynamic properties.
The proposed falsification test compares predicted and experimentally measured melting temperatures and phase fractions for a set of high-entropy alloys.
A significant deviation between predicted and measured melting temperatures and phase fractions would falsify the hypothesis.
